newsitem.title: USA: Military will not abandon high morals - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: Military will not abandon high morals - Cohen.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Cohen on Wednesday attacked calls by critics for the U.S. military to ease stern "Victorian" rules against adultery, lying and other immorality.

In a terse and pointed speech to the Air Force Academy graduating class at Colorado Springs, Colorado, Cohen said American troops must continue to obey standards that are far above those demanded by civilian society in America.

He did not mention specific incidents but made obvious reference to an ongoing Army sex harassment scandal and last week's controversial resignation of the first woman Air Force B-52 pilot to avoid trial on charges of adultery and lying.

"There are some who now suggest that the military is preaching Victorian values in the age of Aquarius, that our standards are unrealistic or even undesirable when contrasted with contemporary mores," Cohen said.

"I disagree," he added in apparent rebuttal of calls from some in Congress to end combined military training of men and women and to ease strict rules against social contact between different ranks, known as "fraternization."
"I believe the reason that our military is the best in the world is that we refuse to accept the least," he said to applause from graduates and senior Air Force military and civilian officials.

Several members of Congress including Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi roundly criticised the Air Force's handling of the case of 1st Lt. Kelly Flinn, forced to resign last week without the honourable discharge that she requested at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota.

"Sometimes members of the force will fall short of our standards," Cohen said. "While harassment, abuse, misconduct have occurred in the ranks, these breaches of faith are the exceptions rather than the rule and they do not paint the true picture of service in the armed forces."
But Cohen told graduates in the academy's football stadium that standards will remain high in the military. His speech was released by the Pentagon in Washington.
